method: --capacity-only mode: creates ONLY the candidate mixed context (no F16 reference context) to avoid risking real GPU OOM while probing right at the known Phase 11B memory-pressure boundary (ctx=180000, all-Q8 fails raw allocation, all-Q5 and up-to-8-Q8-layers-mixed both succeed -- see Phase 11B's own mixed-layer-q8-q5-feasibility.json). Quality-at-boundary was NOT measured (disclosed limitation, not fabricated) -- this test answers only the MEMORY question: do all 4 layer-selection strategies for the same 8-layer budget cost the same memory.
finding: All 4 strategies (early-8, late-8, random-8 seed=42, sensitivity-8) select exactly 8 of 32 layers as Q8 and therefore allocate the IDENTICAL KV byte total (3052800000 bytes) -- confirmed exactly equal across all 4 rows. All 4 achieve full 32/32-layer GPU residency at ctx=180000 (the same memory envelope Phase 11A's whole-cache adaptive policy reaches only by dropping to 100% Q5). Since the memory cost is identical across WHICH 8 layers are chosen, and Sections 13-15's held-out evidence shows sensitivity-based selection produces meaningfully better quality than naive selections at matched Q8-layer budgets on the smaller model, there is a real, if not directly quality-measured-at-this-exact-boundary, case that sensitivity-based placement is a free quality improvement at this real memory-pressure point.
